error_patterns.description: Only 2 test-set error(s) and 0 dev-set error(s) were observed (2 total). Pattern analysis below pools both splits, but conclusions should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size.

This is a classic boundary case: articles involving personal tragedies or community events related to crime may lack explicit legal/judicial vocabulary, causing the classifier to fall back to the catch-all 'Other' category. Documents labeled Crime/Law were predicted as Other. Dominant TF-IDF terms in misclassified samples: "mia", "robin", "detroit", "candles". These terms have high weight in both the gold and predicted categories, confirming lexical overlap as the root cause.

Political corruption, investigations, and ethics probes share vocabulary with crime reporting (e.g., 'grand jury', 'investigation', 'charges'). The classifier cannot distinguish political accountability stories from criminal justice coverage based on bag-of-words features alone. Documents labeled Politics were predicted as Crime/Law. Dominant TF-IDF terms in misclassified samples: "evans", "the ajc", "grand jury", "ajc". These terms have high weight in both the gold and predicted categories, confirming lexical overlap as the root cause.
